title: Distributed instrumentation spec and SDK hooking guidelines
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: define a concise, cross-language specification for lightweight SDK hooks and request-level telemetry that supports deterministic request attribution and safe context propagation across async boundaries. Goals: 1) establish a minimal header/key set for identity and sequence propagation, 2) prescribe SDK hook APIs (start/finish/instrument) that are low-allocation and async-friendly, 3) document sampling deterministic rules and fallbacks, 4) set performance budgets and test signals for rollout, 5) provide migration guidance for legacy instrumentation.
acceptance_criteria: Spec doc published in Confluence with header formats, sampling algorithm, and SDK examples for Node/Go/Python/Java
SDK changes: export hook APIs that match spec and pass language integration tests
Integration tests demonstrate <0.5% increase at p99 latency for common request paths when hooks enabled
End-to-end trace propagation validated across frontend -> edge -> runtime -> downstream services for injected seqid and trace id
Rollout plan with canary percentage gating and dashboard alerts defined
notes: We prefer a single lightweight seq header: X-Redwood-Seq (base36, up to 24 chars) to enable deterministic ordering and cheap cookie-free affinity.
Deterministic sampling algorithm: stable_hash(user_id || route || seqid) mod 10000 < sample_rate*10000. This minimizes sampling bias for stateful routes.

SDK API guidance: provide non-blocking startSpan(ctx, name, opts) returning an immutable handle with finish(err) to minimize allocations. Offer an opt-in context carrier for frameworks that cannot attach to thread-local storage.

Compatibility: Node should support async_hooks-safe context capture, Go should expose context.Context adapter, Python should support contextvars, Java should provide a minimal interface for reactive frameworks.
Header sanitization: only propagate approved attribute whitelist; redact PII by default and provide opt-in allowlist via env var REDWOOD_INSTRUMENTATION_ALLOWLIST.
Performance budget: instrumentation code path must not add >5 allocations on hot path for Node and <2 syscalls for Go in measured microbenchmarks.
Fallbacks: when seq header absent, use monotonic local seq per edge with origin marker to avoid collision; full trace id still required for cross-service joins.
Migration: adapter layer for legacy clients to synthesize seqid from existing request ids and a per-edge salt. Document sample migration steps.

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: header growth causing CDN or proxy truncation. Mitigation: keep seq header <=24 chars and include origin tag to reconstruct if truncated.
Risk: inadvertent PII propagation. Mitigation: default redact and provide explicit allowlist controlled by env var and audited in code review.
Risk: sampling misalignment across services. Mitigation: deterministic sampling algorithm documented and distributed library helpers provided in SDKs.
